title: Emerald Bank - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
next_steps: Run a 2-week pilot with 2 dedicated GPU nodes
Schedule benchmark run (synthetic + prod traffic) w/ Redwood SE
action_items: Ethan Morales: Send pricing and commitment tiers by 2026-11-06
Maya Chen: Share benchmark run plan and sample load script by 2026-11-05
Sofia Reyes: Provide token/sequence distribution and peak qps by 2026-11-06
Raj Kapoor: Confirm VPC peering requirements and network egress constraints by 2026-11-09
summary: Discovery with Emerald Bank focused on Dedicated capacity. Customer wants reserved GPUs in a private VPC, predictable throughput, and a burst strategy for seasonal peaks. Key concerns: data isolation, SOC2, latency SLAs, cost vs hosting, and scaling rules. Agreed next steps include pricing, SOC2/network docs, and a benchmark pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Ethan Morales from Redwood, with me is Maya Chen our SE. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Kevin (Emerald - CTO): Good, thanks Ethan. we have about an hour, want to dive into our infra needs.
[00:12] Maya (Redwood SE): Great, quick agenda — understand workload, infra constraints, security needs, and then discuss Dedicated options and a pilot.
[00:18] Raj (Infra): Sounds good. we run models for document ingestion and conversational banking assistant. peak times at month-end and payroll cycles, those cause bursts.
[00:27] Sofia (Lead ML): Our average prompt token length is 800 to 1,400 tokens, but we do shorter queries as well. latency target around 300-400 ms p50 for simple retrieval+generate flows, p95 we want under 1s ideally.
[00:38] Ethan: ok gotcha. are you currently self-hosted or using any hosted LLM API?
[00:42] Kevin: We're on a mix — some RAG pipelines on a hosted provider for experiments, most production inference is on-prem GPU clusters managed by infra. costs spiking and maintenance is heavy, so looking at a Dedicated reserved option.
[00:54] Maya: when you say Dedicated, we offer reserved GPU pools in a private VPC with optional burst capacity to our shared fleet. that would give you isolation and predictable throughput; you can also configure canary/rollout policies.
[01:05] Sofia: how does burst work — we need guaranteed capacity for peak windows but can't afford to overprovision 24/7.
[01:10] Maya: common pattern: commit to baseline reserved nodes (e.g., N GPUs) sized for normal load, plus burst to Redwood shared capacity for spikes. bursts are throttled by policy and compatible model variants; if your model is quantized or faster variant we can route automatically.
[01:22] Raj: network-wise we need VPC peering and IP allowlist, also strict egress controls — can you support private peering and no public internet egress for payloads?
[01:28] Ethan: yes, our Dedicated product supports VPC peering and private control plane options — can be set up so inference traffic doesn't traverse public internet. we also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[01:36] Lena (Security): SOC2 is a must. do you have audit logs, RBAC, SSO,SAML?
[01:41] Ethan: yes SOC2 Type II, SSO with SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and detailed audit logs. we'll share the security pack.
[01:48] Kevin: what about model pinning and version rollouts — we need deterministic outputs for regulatory tests.
[01:53] Maya: you can pin model versions per route and do canary rollouts. fallback policies can route to an alternative variant if capacity is constrained. that keeps determinism.
[02:01] Sofia: what's the autoscaling granularity? we don't want cold starts to introduce latency.
[02:05] Maya: autoscaling is GPU-level; we manage pre-warm and continuous batching to reduce cold start surface. for Dedicated you can define min GPU nodes and warm pools; the runtime uses KV cache to keep hot prefixes in memory.
[02:16] Raj: are we able to run on specific GPU types? For compliance we prefer NVIDIA H100, or A100 at least.
[02:22] Ethan: yes we can provision specific instance types for Dedicated commitments — H100/A100 depending on region and availability. pricing differs by GPU SKU.
[02:28] Kevin: cost — can you share ballpark numbers? we have finance constraints and will compare to our on-prem TCO.
[02:33] Ethan: we'll send a pricing sheet with commitment tiers. Typical structure: baseline reserved monthly cost by GPU + usage for burst and per-token charges for hosted components. we'll include comparison scenarios.
[02:43] Sofia: performance — can you run benchmarks with our model or a close open model? we need p50/p95 numbers at our token distributions.
[02:49] Maya: yes SE can run an in-house benchmark or we can run one in partnership; we'll need your token/sequence distribution and representative payloads. can simulate peak qps.
[02:58] Mark (PM): timeline — if we move forward, how long to provision Dedicated?
[03:02] Ethan: baseline provisioning for Dedicated in a new account/VPC is roughly 2-4 weeks end-to-end — includes security review, network setup, and GPU allocation. pilot can start faster with limited capacity.
[03:10] Raj: what's the SLA for uptime and latency?
[03:13] Ethan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on request; we'll include specific SLO language in the enterprise contract.
[03:19] Sofia: any limitations on long-running contexts or KV cache sizes? some of our flows maintain multi-turn histories up to 8k tokens.
[03:25] Maya: runtime supports long contexts but effective throughput depends on model and quantization. KV cache management is tunable; we can configure cache eviction policies to fit your workloads.
[03:34] Kevin: security question — can we run private control plane inside our VPC or is it managed?
[03:39] Ethan: we offer a private control plane for enterprise customers as an option; that can be deployed in your environment with strict network controls, or we can do VPC peering with our managed control plane.
[03:48] Raj: for burst — are there throttles or queueing? we need predictable tails.
[03:52] Maya: burst uses capacity pools and policy-based routing. during bursts requests may be queued or routed to compatible lower-cost variants; you can set hard limits to avoid cost runaway. we also expose per-token cost telemetry to help tune policies.
[04:04] Sofia: how do we handle model updates and regression detection?
[04:08] Maya: Redwood Optimize offers quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can set evaluation prompts and get alerts when metrics drift.
[04:15] Mark: what's required from us to run the pilot?
[04:18] Ethan: provide sample payloads, token distribution, expected peak qps, and list of critical routes. we'll propose a 2-week pilot on 2 dedicated GPUs with a benchmark script.
[04:26] Lena: any GDPR/data residency concerns? we need EU region tenancy for some data.
[04:30] Ethan: yes you can pin region and we support data residency controls; the private deployment option can be used for stricter residency.
[04:36] Kevin: ok, summary — we want baseline reserved GPUs, burst to shared pool, private VPC peering, SOC2 docs, and a benchmark pilot.
[04:43] Ethan: perfect, we'll send pricing, SOC2/security pack, and a benchmark plan. Maya will run the benchmark with your data.
[04:49] Sofia: one more question — encryption keys, can Redwood integrate with our KMS/HSM?
[04:53] Maya: yes customer-managed keys supported; HSM integrations possible depending on the plan.
[04:57] Raj: network egress costs — any surprises?
[05:00] Ethan: outbound egress depends on region and your network path; we'll include an estimate. dedicated deployments typically reduce overall egress via VPC peering.
[05:08] Mark: ok thanks everyone.
[05:10] Ethan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the pack and next steps.
[05:13] Kevin: thanks, talk soon.
[05:15] END
